title: Clone as Internal Shape
content: **Clone as Internal Shape** \- Create an Internal Shape identical to a Pattern. \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021849587/mceclip0.png) **Transform pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911008/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right click on the desired pattern and select **Clone as Internal Shape.** \- The duplicated Internal Shape will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the 2D window to paste the duplicated Internal Shape. \- The selected Pattern will be cloned as an Internal Shape.
content_description: Learn how to easily clone a pattern as an Internal Shape in your design software by using the Transform or Edit Pattern tools.

title: Colorway Multiview Snapshot
content: **List of Contents** Colorway Multiview Snapshot Capturing Colorway Multiview Snapshot **Colorway Multiview Snapshot ** \- Capture multiview snapshot of a single garment or an outfit in multiple colorways at one time. \- Switch to Colorway Mode. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ FILE ▶ Snapshot ▶ **3D Window** to create and save a Snapshot. **Capturing Colorway Multiview Snapshot ** \- Switch to Colorway Mode and navigate to File ▶ Snapshot ▶**3D Window**. \- A file browser will appear. \- Assign file name and its saving location. Then, select Save. \- Snapshot pop-up window will appear. \- Check **Save All Colorways** under Options category. Select Save. \- Multiview snapshot of the 3D Garment in multiple colorways will be saved at the designated location. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for capturing and saving multiview snapshots of garments in various colorways using the Colorway Multiview Snapshot feature.

title: Custom View
content: **List of Contents** Add Open/Save Overwrite/Rename/Delete #### Easily open and save custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. #### #### **Add** 1. Right-click on the 3D background and click **Custom View** menu. 2. Click ![camera.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824664985) **Add Current Viewpoint** in Custom View window. 3. Click on the added custom view to instantly switch to it. #### #### **Open/Save** 1. Click ![Button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824666137) **Save** / ![Button-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44249824667033) **Open** to manage Custom Views as ZCMR file. #### #### **Overwrite/Rename/Delete** 1. Right-click on the added custom view 2. Right-click on the added Custom View to overwrite it with the current view, rename it, or delete it. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on managing custom views in the 3D window, including how to add, open, save, overwrite, rename, and delete viewpoints for enhanced user convenience.

title: 3D Garment View Controls
content: **List of Contents** Change Camera View Zoom In/Out Shortcuts Zoom to Selected Zoom in and change view in the 3D window at once. **Change Camera View** Right click on the 3D window to access the pop-up menu. Select the desired view among Front, 3/4 Left, Back, Left, Right, 3/4 Right, Top, Button, or use respective shortcuts (2, 3, 8, 6, 4, 1, 5, 0) to change camera view instantly. **Camera Direction Change Standards** Using the corresponding menu while the avatar is facing a different direction on the screen changes the camera's angle according to the avatar. **Zoom In/Out Shortcuts** **Zoom In:** Hold down the + key on the keyboard to zoom in the 3D window. **Zoom Out:** Hold down the - key on the keyboard to zoom out the 3D window. **Zoom to Selected** Zoom in/out and rotate the 3D window using the selected Pattern or item as the focal point. Select the desired Pattern or item in the 3D window and locate Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ **Zoom Extends All** , Or press the shortcut key F to enlarge the selected object at a fixed scale at the middle and control the view according to it. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for navigating and manipulating camera views and zoom functions within a 3D window environment.

title: Show/Hide Seam Allowance
content: ### **Objective** Show or hide seam allowances from the 2D window. Seam allowances can be shown and hidden in the Print Layout Mode as well. ** Location ** **For versions 5.0 and later:** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Show Seam Allowance** 2D Window ▶ 2D Pattern Display ▶ **Show Seam Allowance** **For versions 4.2 and earlier:** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern**** **2D Toolbar ▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36783351426329) **Transform Pattern** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated location above based on your software version: 2. For **versions 5.0 and later** , follow the path to the option either through the main menu or the vertical toggle bar in the 2D window. The seam allowances can be hidden again using the same path. 3. For **versions 4.2 and earlier** , right-click into the empty space of the 2D window: → In the right-click menu, select**Show Seam Allowance**. Repeat this to hide seam allowances again. **※Note:** All seam allowances remain shown when the ![seam_allowance.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36783335099545) **Seam Allowance** tool is activated.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to show or hide seam allowances in the 2D window for different versions of the software.

title: [CLO-SET] Upload to CLO-SET
content: ### **Objective** Upload 3D files and share them easily with others. ** Location ** Main Menu ▶ CLO-SET ▶ Upload to CLO-SET ▶ **Project/Garment/Avatar** ** Operation** 1. Create a project. 2. Follow the location outlined above. → You will be directed to the upload page on CLO-SET. → For **Network OnlineAuth** users: If you are not a registered member of CLO-SET, you are directed to the sign up page. **※ Note:** For detailed instruction on how to use CLO-SET, please refer to the **[CLO-SET Help Center](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/categories/4405849186447-GETTING-STARTED)**.

title: Assign to New Fabric
content: **Assign to New Fabric** * **Assign to New Fabric ** \- Add a new fabric item and apply it to the selected Patterns simultaneously. \- Select Patterns using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021908028/mceclip0.png) Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the Patterns to access the pop-up menu. Select **Assign to New Fabric.** A new fabric item will be added and applied to the selected Patterns.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide instructions for adding a new fabric item and applying it to selected patterns in the design tool.

title: Optimize All Curve Points
content: **Optimize All Curve Points** \- Easily edit curves by optimizing the number of curve points on segments. Use this function when there are unnecessarily many curve points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022574027/mceclip0.png) **Edit Curve Point** tool from the 2D toolbar to see all curve points on Patterns. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Optimize All Curve Points** from the pop-up menu. Surplus curve points will be deleted and only the necessary curve points needed to maintain the shape of the curves will be remained.
content_description: "Streamline your design process by optimizing curve points to enhance efficiency and maintain the integrity of your patterns."

title: V-Ray Render Image/Video Properties
content: **List of Contents** Image/Video Properties Image/Video Image Size Color Correction Background Save Open/Save Image/Video Properties **Image/Video Properties ** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026473148/mceclip0.png) **Image/Video Properties** tool from the Render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Image/Video ** \- Select the medium for the final Render product among Image, Turntable Images, and Turntable Video. * **Image** \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as an image. * **View Point** * **Current View** \- Render the 3D Garment as it is shown in the 3D window. * **Custom View** \- Render the 3D Garment with a Custom View. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Images ** \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as multiple images, showing it in 360°. * **Image Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered. \- Higher the Image Count is, from more viewpoints the 3D Garment is rendered. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). * **Turntable Video** \- Extract rendered 3D Garment as a video rotating in 360° * **Video Frame Count** \- Decide the number of images to be rendered and stitched as a video. \- Higher the Video Frame Count, more smoothly the video rotates. * **Duration** \- Decide the total duration of the video. \- Expand the child menu to find Video Frame Duration, which decides the duration per frame. * **Direction** * **Counterclockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered counterclockwise. * **Clockwise** \- The 3D Garment is rendered clockwise. * **Video Codec** \- Select the video codec used for recording. * **Render All Colorways** All Colorways from the Colorway Mode are rendered(ver4.1.0). **Image Size ** \- Set the dimension of rendered images or videos. \- Choose among provided presets or select Custom to freely configure the width and height of the images or videos as needed. * **Orientation** * **Portrait** \- The image is laid out vertically. * **Landscape** \- The image is laid out horizontally. * **Width** \- Set image’s width * **Height** \- Set image’s height * **Maintain Ratio** \- Lock Width and Height ratio by toggling on the Maintain Ratio option. **Color Correction ** * **Exposure** \- Set how much the image is exposed to light. \- Higher the Exposure value is, brighter the image is. * **Contrast** \- Set how strong the bright and dark areas are contrasted. \- Higher the Contrast value is, stronger the contrast gets. **Background ** * **Color** \- Set the color of the background. * **Transparency** \- Set the background image as transparent. **Save ** * **File Name** \- Decide the name of the saved images. * **File Path** \- Locate the saving path for the images. **Open/Save Image/Video Properties ** * **Open** \- Open previously saved Image/Video Properties. * **Save** \- Save configured Image/Video Properties and apply to other files. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to configuring and rendering image and video properties for 3D garments, detailing options for size, color correction, and saving preferences.

title: Linked Editing
content: **List of Contents** Set Linked Editing Remove Linked Editing #### **You can set linked editing to edit the pattern more quickly and efficiently. ** #### **Set Linked Editing** **Symmetric Pattern** 1. Right-click on the pattern to clone it symmetrically with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)****Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶ **Symmetric Pattern (with Sewing)/Symmetric Pattern'** menu. 3. Click on the 2D window to arragne the clone. **Instance Pattern** 1. Right-click on the pattern to clone it as an instance with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on 'Clone Pattern with Linked Editing ▶**Instance Pattern'** menu. 3. Click on the 2D window to arrange the clone, or right-click on the 2D window while arranging to set the number of shapes and define the interval. **📝****Note:** Right-click on both patterns that are not linked and select the '**Apply Linked Editing** ' menu to apply linked editing without cloning. #### #### **Remove Linked Editing** 1. Right-click on the pattern to remove linked editing with **![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866981223577)Transform Pattern** tool. 2. Click on the '**Remove Linked Eidting** ' menu. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37866999702937) ### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38097968974361) Linked editing can be removed only for the internal lines within a pattern, while keeping linked editing for the overall pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on setting and removing linked editing for patterns to enhance editing efficiency in your design workflow.

Double-click the file to load it. → The file will be loaded. ****📝****Note:**** You can open or [add previous versions of CLO-SET files](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/360002199235-Content-Version-Upload) directly in CLO by right-clicking on the file thumbnail. (ver 2024.1)

Button Metal Preset.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39592727165721)

title: Open/Save Fabric File
content: ### **Objective** Save a frequently used Fabric as a .zfab file or open a saved Fabric file to reuse. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ **Open** /**Save** ### **Operation ** **General** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click the fabric item and the Open/Save button in the Property Editor. → The Save Fabric window will appear when saving. **옵션** | **설명** ---|--- **Preview Image** | Texture Image is applied by default, It can be set to Custom Image. **Texture Image (ver 2024.1)** | If the texture image has transparency, choose to include or remove the transparency. 3. After setting the save options, click the OK button to save. → The fabric will be saved as a ZFAB file with the selected options. → The fabric with the sel properties will be saved as a ZFAB file. **Select Material** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the fabric item ▶ Click the Open (Select Material) menu. → Load Fabric window appears. 3. Select a Zfab file. → Open Fabric window appears. 4. Select the items desired and click the OK button. → The selected items are reflected in the fabric properties. ****📝** Note: ** Press **Ctrl** on the keyboard while dragging and dropping the fabric file to the fabric item to open the 'Select Material window'.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and opening Fabric files as .zfab formats to streamline your design workflow.

title: Create POM
content: **List of Contents** Single Group **Objective** Create rulers to check measurements of particular parts of 2D Patterns/Internal Shapes/Graphics. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pattern Measure ▶ **Point of Measure** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![pom.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039947034) **Point of Measure** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. ** ** 2. Left-click on a **pattern or internal line** to start creating a ruler. ** ** **Single ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A single POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab. **Group ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A group POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab as a single measurement. → The length of the line linking two Patterns (one that is not placed within Patterns) is not included in the measurement. **📝****Note****:** * Hold down the Shift key to display vertical, horizontal, and 45º guidelines based on the clicked point. * To cancel while creating POM, press down the backspace key, ESC or Ctrl+Z (Windows)/Cmd+Z (Mac) keys on the keyboard. * While creating POM, right-click to enter Distance Moved. * Check 3D Length in the Property Editor after creating POM. * Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines can be [traced as POM.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728-Trace) * If there is grading information in the pattern that created the tape measure, the length is displayed by grading size in the POM tab. * When creating a POM, press the **P** key on the keyboard to switch between the mode for generating it along a segment line and the mode for generating it as a polygon.(ver 2024.1) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the Point of Measure (POM) tool in 2D pattern design to accurately create and manage measurement rulers for various graphics and shapes.

title: V-Ray Render Light Properties
content: **List of Contents** Light Properties Environment Map Light Intensity Rectangle Light Open/Save Settings **Light Properties **\- Set lighting properties applied to final render output. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026363368/mceclip0.png) **Light Properties** tool from the render toolbar and navigate to the Property Editor. ** Environment Map **\- The **environment map** is a lighting setting processed into an image format. \- By default, six different environment maps are provided. \- Select the desired environment map as needed. **Light Intensity ** \- Adjust the brightness of the 3D Garment in the final rendered image by configuring the Light Intensity. \- The default value is 1.00 and the setting can be adjusted between 0.00 and 4.00. \- Higher the value is, brighter the 3D Garment is. **Rectangle Light ** \- Add and modify point lights up to three. \- Adjust lights' location with the Gizmo tool. * **Intensity ** \- Adjust the intensity of the light. * **Color ** \- Set the color of the light. * **Width ** \- Set the width of the light. * **Height ** \- Set the height of the light. * **Show ** \- Show or hide the light from the 3D window. **※ Note :** * To create a three-dimensional render image, there must be a key light. Add key lights as needed to create more dynamic images. * When the Rectangle Lights are used along with the Dome Light, use a HDRI image without a key light. **Open/Save Settings ** * **Open ** \- Click the Open button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to load previously saved Light Properties. * **Save ** \- Click the Save button on the right top corner of the Property Editor to save the configuration. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions and settings for adjusting light properties in 3D rendering, including environment maps, light intensity, and rectangle light configurations.

title: Realistic Knitwear Designer
content: **Create realistic knitwear with a variety of stitchings. ** ### 1. Click the Fabric in Fabric tab in Object Browser, and then Change the Material Type to Knitwear in Property Editor. 2. Adjust each detail property to express the desired knitwear. **Properties** | **Description**** ** ---|--- **Stitching** | Set the knit's Stitching type. **Yarn Thickness** | Set the thickness of the yarn. **Gauge** | Gauge refers to the number of knitting stitches within an inch. This means you can control the size of a stitch in the knit fabric: Higher values represent denser, thinner knits, and lower values represent thicker knits. **Knit Direction ** | Adjust the Knit Direction. **Ply Amount** | Set the number of threads for plying. **Ply Randomization** **(Melange)**** ** | Plying is randomly blended to create a natural melange effect. **Randomization Factor** | Adjust the density of the plying. Higher values result in a denser appearance. **Seed Position** | Adjust the position of the plying. **Yarn Variance************ **| ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40169904800409) **Irreqularity** | **Scale** | Adjust how much the yarn randomly moves. **Frequency** | Adjust how often the yarn direction changes. **Pilling** | **Length (mm)** | Adjust how short or long the fluff can get. Higher values result in a longer pilling appearance. **Thickness** | Adjust how thick the fluff can get. Higher values result in a thicker pilling appearance. **Frequency** | Adjust how often the fluff appears. **Generate Seams** | Additional yarn is created along the seam lines and pattern outlines. If the seams of the knitwear pattern are unnatural, adjust the option to make them look natural. **Ply Normal Map** | Apply the normal map to the plying to express the three-dimensional effect of the yarn. **Ply Color** | Set the color for each yarn in the plying. ****📝 Note:** ** * It may affect performance and speed when applying knitwear, and you can turn off the **![Garment Surface Textured Thick Normal.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29738213752217)****Garment Rendering Style** in 3D window ▶ ![Garment Option Kintwear Mesh.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29738213766041)**Show Knitwear** during other operations to work at the same speed as before. * To optimize the knitwear mesh in the invisible camera area of the final rendered image, apply the settings in [Render Properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties) ▶ Mesh Optimization.
content_description: Discover how to create lifelike knitwear by customizing stitch types, yarn thickness, and plying effects for a truly unique design.

title: Transform Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Transform Pattern Select Pattern Select Multiple Patterns Move Pattern Scale Pattern Rotate Pattern **Transform Pattern** \- Select, move, and scale Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022750927/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Tranform Pattern.** ** Select Pattern** * **Click ** \- Click within the pattern to be selected. \- Or, create a marquee box to encompass the Patterns to be selected. Keep in mind that the Patterns need to be fully enclosed within the marquee box in order to be selected properly. * **Lasso Selection ** \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the Patterns to be selected to draw marquee box in a desired shape and click the start point again the complete the Lasso Selection. \- The selected Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. \- Similar with selecting Patterns with the marquee box, Patterns should be fully enclosed. **Select Multiple Patterns** \- While selecting Patterns, hold down the Shift key and select all Patterns you desire to select. **Move Pattern** * **With Mouse ** \- Click and drag the Pattern. * **With Arrow Keys ** \- Click the Pattern to be moved. \- Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the Pattern towards the desired direction. \- The Pattern will move in 1cm increments when using the arrow keys on the keyboard. * **Move in Guidelines ** \- While click and dragging the Pattern, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. \- The Pattern can be moved in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Scale Pattern** * **Scale Manually ** \- Click the Pattern to be scaled. The marquee box will appear around the Pattern. \- Click and drag the white point on the marquee box to enlarge or shrink the selected Pattern. * **Scale with Specific Values ** \- After selecting the Pattern and click and dragging the white point on the marquee box, right click on the 2D window. \- The Transform window will appear. \- Enter the desired values to Percentage and Dimension to scale the Pattern with the desired values. **Rotate Pattern ** \- Click on the Pattern to show the marquee box. \- Click and drag the white point above the marquee box to rotate the selected Pattern. * **Pivot Point** \- The point at the center of the Pattern appears with the marquee box is the Pivot Point. \- Double click the Pivot Point to activate it. 。 \- Move the Pivot Point to change the fiducial point which the Pattern will rotate on the basis of. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions on how to select, move, scale, and rotate patterns using the Transform Pattern tool in a 2D design environment.

title: PBR Map Generator (ver 2024.1)
content: ### **Objective** Generate PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness Maps) for realistic texture expresssion from a basic texture image. **Location ** Texture Property Editor ▶ Each PBR Map Properties ▶ ![PBR.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33852438547481)**PBR Map Generator** ** Operation** 1. Load a texture image from the object properties whose [fabric](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) and material you want to change. 2. Select the tool/menu in Location. → Each PBR map is automatically generated based on the texture image.
content_description: Create realistic PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness) effortlessly from a basic texture image using our intuitive PBR Map Generator.

title: Create Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Ellipse Create Ellipse **Ellipse** \- Create Ellipse or circle in 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar. ** Create Ellipse** * **Free-hand an Ellipse ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click and drag on the 2D window as the preview of an Ellipse appears. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a Circle. \- When the desired shape of an Ellipse or a Circle is achieved, release the mouse. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Diameter & Radius **\- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. ** -** Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse Window appears. \- Enter desired values for**Width** ,**Height** , **Diameter** , and**Radius**. Then, hit OK. \- An Ellipse or a Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. * **Use Circumference ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- Enter desired values for **Circumference.** \- An Ellipse or Circle Pattern is created based on the settings. ** ** * **Create and Replicate Ellipses ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021379368/mceclip0.png) **Ellipse** tool from the 2D toolbar, and then navigate to the 2D window. \- Click on the 2D window. The Create Ellipse window appears. \- **Interval** : type in the distance between the Ellipses. \- **Angle** : type in the angle that replicated Ellipses will be created. \- **Number of Shapes** : type in the number of Ellipses to be replicated. \- Click OK. \- The Ellipses are created based on the settings above. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create and manipulate ellipses and circles in a 2D window using the Ellipse tool.

title: Slash and Spread
content: **List of Contents** Slash and Spread Create Slash Line Rotate Pattern **Slash and Spread** \- Create a Slash Line inside a Pattern to divide, rotate, and edit the Pattern. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022743268/mceclip0.png) **Slash &Spread** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Patterns ▶ Edit ▶**Slash &Spread.** ** Create Slash Line** \- To divide and rotate the Patterns, the Slash Line must be created first. \- The Slash Line can be created on the Pattern outlines. \- Click on the Pattern outline to create the start point. The start point of the Slash Line will be the fiducial point where the Pattern will rotated on the basis of. Drag the mouse on click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used as Slash Lines. 。 **Rotate Pattern** \- Click the half of the Pattern that will be rotated. Hover the mouse over the half and when the Pattern is highlighted in light-blue, click to select. When the half of the Pattern is selected, it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Move the mouse cursor to preview the Pattern after the modification. Rotate the Pattern to spread or clip Patterns. \- Move the half of the Pattern as desired and click to complete the modification. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used to rotate Patterns. \- Or, when moving the half of the Pattern, right-click to access the Spread window. Enter the desired values to Distance and Angle and click OK. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Slash and Spread tool to create, divide, and rotate patterns in design software.

title: Add Point/Split Line
content: **List of Contents** Add Point/Split Line Add Point Split into Two Lines Split by Length Uniform Split **Add Point/ Split Line** \- Add point to Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to split them. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Add Point/Split Line.** ** Add Point** \- Add point to Pattern outlines. \- Add point to Internal Lines. **Split into Two Lines** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split into Two Lines. ** \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The desired length can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. \- The selected line will be divided into two different length segments on the basis of the purple guide point. The proportion of each segment can be entered in the Line 1, the shorter segment and the Line 2, the longer segment. **Split by Length** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/ Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Split by Length. ** \- **Segment Length** : points will be added to the line with the Segment Length Interval, starting from one side of the line. \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be divided into. \- **Direction** : set toward which direction the points will be added. **Uniform Split** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021155167/mceclip0.png) **Add Point/Split Line** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, right click on a segment and select **Split. ** \- The Split Line window will appear. Click **Uniform Split. ** \- **Number of Segments** : set how many segments the line will be equally divided into. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Add Point/Split Line tool in 2D pattern editing, detailing methods for adding points and splitting lines into various configurations.

title: Edit Piping
content: **List of Contents** Edit Piping Select Piping Edit Length Edit Piping Properties Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu **Edit Piping** \- Select and edit Pipings on 3D Garments. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Piping ▶ **Edit Piping** ** ****Select Piping** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click on the Piping on the 3D Garment. \- The selected Piping will be highlighted in yellow. **Edit Length** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool selected, click and drag either end of the Piping towards the direction it will be abridged or extended. **Edit Piping Properties** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the **Select/Move** , click the Piping on the 3D Garment and navigate the Property Editor. \- The selected Piping’s properties will appear. * **Name** \- View and edit the name of the selected Piping. * **Line Length** \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Width** \- View the length of the selected Piping. * **Particle Distance** \- View and edit the Particle Distance of the selected Piping. \- The Piping’s Particle Distance is set as 1.5mm by default. \- Narrower the Piping’s width is, smaller the Particle Distance should be. * **Hide** \- Toggle on or off the **Hide** checkbox to hide or show the selected Piping. \- The Piping will appear translucent when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. * **Fabric** \- Change the fabric material for the selected Piping. \- The options appear in the list are the fabric lists in the Object Browser. **Piping Right Click Pop-Up Menu** \- With the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022184048/mceclip1.png) **Select/Move** tool, right click on the Piping to access the right-click pop-up menu. * **Delete** \- Delete the selected Piping. \- Select the Piping and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. * **Refresh All Piping** \- Re-drape all Pipings on the 3D Garment. \- Use this to re-simulate Pipings that distorted while simulating the 3D Garment. * **Deactivate** \- Deactivate the selected Piping. \- Right-click again on the deactivated piping. The **Deactivate** option should have changed to the **Activate** option. Select **Activate** to activate the piping. * **Freeze** \- Freeze the piping to exclude it from the simulation. \- Right-click again on the frozen piping. The **Freeze** option should have changed to the **Unfreeze** option. Select **Unfreeze** to unfreeze the piping. * **Quadrangulate** \- Change the Piping’s mesh structure to rectangles. * **Triangulate** \- Change the Piping’s mesh structure to triangles. * **Hide** \- Hide the selected Piping. \- The Piping wiil appear translucent when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool is activated, but it will disappear when other 3D tools are activated. \- To show the hidden Piping, select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022123967/mceclip0.png) **Edit Piping** tool and right click on the Piping. The **Hide** option should have changed to the **Show** option. \- Select the **Show** option to show the selected Piping. * **Show All Piping -** Show all hidden Pipings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to select and edit piping properties in 3D garments using the Edit Piping tool, including options for adjusting length, managing visibility, and accessing additional features through the right-click pop-up menu.

title: Fasten Button
content: **List of Contents** Fasten Button Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes Unfastening Buttons and Buttonholes **Fasten Button ** \- Fasten buttons and buttonholes on 3D Garment. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026624868/mceclip0.png) **Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. **Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes** * **Fasten a Single Pair ** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026624868/mceclip0.png) **Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent and both buttons and buttonholes can be easily identified. \- Either in the 2D or the 3D Window, click on the button to be fastened. \- Then, click on the buttonhole that the button will be fastened to. \- The selected button and the buttonhole will be fastened when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026624928/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** is activated as the button simulates above the buttonhole. \- If the selected button and the buttonhole are fastened properly, a lock icon will hover over the button. * **Fasten Multiple Pairs **\- To fasten multiple buttons at once, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all buttons to be fastened. \- Click the first buttonhole of the collection which selected buttons are paired. **Unfastening Buttons and Buttonholes** * **Unfasten a Singe Pair ** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026624868/mceclip0.png) **Fasten Button** tool from the 3D Toolbar. \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent and both buttons and buttonholes can be easily identified. \- Select on the button or buttonhole to be unfastened either in the 2D or the 3D Window. \- The lock icon will disappear and the Garment will simulate unfastened. * **Unfasten Multiple Pairs ** \- To unfasten multiple pairs of buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on the 2D window to select all buttons to be unfastened. \- Selected buttons are unfastened at once. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to fasten and unfasten buttons and buttonholes in a 3D garment design environment.

title: Buttonhole
content: **List of Contents** Buttonhole Creating a Buttonhole **Buttonhole** \- Create Buttonholes on 3D garment. \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. **Creating a Buttonhole** * **Create a Buttonhole Manually ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to either the 3D Window or the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as a red dot appears to guide the location. \- Click on the desired location to create a Buttonhole. * **Create a Buttonhole with Designated Values ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001028728/Toolbar_3D_Button_Hole.png)**Buttonhole** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as smart guidelines appear. \- Right-click on the desired location to access a pop-up window. The Moving Distance Window will appear. \- Enter the desired value in Distance Moved to move the Buttonhole towards right. \- Enter the desired value in Position to specifically locate the Buttonhole. \- Select OK to complete creating a Buttonhole. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating buttonholes on 3D garments using the designated tools in Clo3D.

title: Button
content: **List of Contents** Button Creating a Button **Button** **** \- Create Buttons on 3D garment. \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001040967/Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png)**Button** tool from the 3D toolbar. **Creating a Button** * **Create a Button Manually ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001040967/Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png)**Button** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to either the 3D Window or the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Button will be created as a red dot appears to guide the location. \- Click on the desired location to create a Button. * **Create a Button with Designated Values ** \- Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001040967/Toolbar_3D_Button_Add.png)**Button** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Button will be created as smart guidelines appear. \- Right-click on the desired location to access a pop-up window. The Moving Distance Window will appear. \- Enter the desired value in Distance Moved to move the Button towards right. \- Enter the desired value in Position to specifically locate the Button. \- Select OK to complete creating a Button. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to create buttons on 3D garments using the CLO 3D software.

title: Select/Move Button
content: **List of Contents** Select/Move Button Moving Buttons Moving Buttonholes Rotating Buttons/Buttonholes Adjusting Thread Length Editing Buttonhole Bind Position Changing Button/Buttonhole Item Button Collision **Select/Move Button** \- Select or move buttons or buttonholes in the 2D and the 3D Window. \- Choose the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)**Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Window. **Moving Buttons** * **3D Window** \- Choose the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)**Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Window. \- Navigate to the 3D Window. Then, click and drag the button to be moved. \- To easily and precisely move or rotate the button, click on the button to access the **Gizmo** tool. \- Click and drag green arrow to move the button vertically; click and drag red arrow to move the button horizontally. \- Click the blue arrow and drag downwards to pull the button forwards; click the blue arrow and drag upwards to push the button backwards. \- Click and drag the yellow box to move the button freely. \- Click and drag the green circle to rotate the button in X-axis; click and drag the red circle to rotate the button in Y-axis. \- Click and drag the blue circle clockwise or counterclockwise to rotate the button respectively. * **2D Window** \- Choose the**![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Window and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Click and drag the button to be moved. \- To move the button with specific values, click and drag the button, and then while holding down the left button of the mouse, right click once. \- When the **Moving Distance** Window appears, enter the desired values in Distance Moved or Position to designate the location. **Moving Buttonholes** \- Choose the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)**Select/Move Button** tool from the 3D Window. \- Navigate to the 2D or the 3D Window to select the buttonhole to be moved. \- Click and drag to move the buttonhole freely. \- In the 2D Window, right click while moving the buttonhole to access the **Moving Distance** Window. \- When the **Moving Distance** Window appears, enter the desired values in Distance Moved or Position to designate the location. **Rotating Buttons/Buttonholes** * **Button**** ** \- With the![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)**Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the button to be rotated. \- The selected button’s property will appear in the Property Editor. \- Enter the desired value in Angle to rotate the button. \- Or, click on the button in the 3D Window. Then, rotate the button using the **Gizmo** tool. * **Buttonhole ** \- With the ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)**Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be rotated. \- The selected buttonhole’s property will appear in the Property Editor. \- Enter the desired value in **Angle** to rotate the buttonhole. **Adjusting Thread Length** \- With the**![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the button to be edited. \- In the Property Editor, the selected button’s property will appear. \- Enter the desired value in **Thread Length** to adjust the offset distance between the button and the 3D garment. **Editing Buttonhole Bind Position ** \- With the **![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)****Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be edited. \- In the Property Editor, the selected buttonhole’s property will appear. \- Adjust **Bind Position** to decide on which edge of the buttonhole the button will be fastened to. **Changing Button/Buttonhole Item** * **Button Item** \- With the **![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)****Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the button to be edited. \- In the Property Editor, the selected button’s property will appear. \- Expand the **Style** drop down menu and choose desired button item. * **Buttonhole Item** \- With the **![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)****Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the buttonhole to be edited. \- In the Property Editor, the selected buttonhole’s property will appear. \- Expand the **Style** drop down menu and choose desired buttonhole item. **Button Collision** \- With the **![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001026727/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png)****Select/Move Button** tool selected, click on the button to be edited. \- In the Property Editor, the selected button’s property will appear. \- Toggle on/off **Collision**. \- When Collision is turned off, the selected button will not be calculated for collision and be fixed at the location that the button was created. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for selecting, moving, and editing buttons and buttonholes in both 2D and 3D design environments.

title: Register Pose/Motion
content: ## **New in 2024.2** #### **You can easily register the pose or motion from an FBX file as a file compatible with CLO avatars. ![Register Pose.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38075492713753) ** #### 1. Click the Main Menu » Avatar » **Register Pose/Motion** menu. 2. Select the type to register, either **Pose** or **Motion**. 3. Open the FBX file by clicking on the ![open.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38075383168153) **Open** button. 4. Select the Gender of the compatible CLO avatar and select the Shoe Type for female. **📝****Note:** If the FBX file's joint names do not match the CLO avatar's, it can only be saved and cannot be registered as the CLO-compatible file. 5. For motion, switch to Animation mode to play loaded motion as needed. 6. Click the **Save** button to save as the Pose(POS) or Motion(MTN) file.
content_description: Discover how to effortlessly register poses and motions from FBX files for CLO avatars in the latest 2024.2 update.

title: Buttonhole Properties
content: **Adjust buttonhole properties such as Transformation and 2D Measurements. ** #### 1. Click on the Buttonhole using the ![Edit Button On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38020483609497) **Select/Move Button** tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Adjust the Buttonhole properties. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Style** | Select a buttonhole style. **Buttonhole** **Transformation****** | **Angle** | Enter the desired value for Rotation Angle of buttonholes. **Z-Offset** | ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38044041419033) Even when the buttonhole is hidden due to additional thickness and displacement maps on fabrics, adjusting the Z-Offset can make it visible. **Bind Position** | Change the bind position of the buttonhole by percentage (%). It can also be entered in units of the program setting. **2D Measurement** | Check the position of the buttonhole in the 2D pattern (left/right/top/bottom) with Measurement.
content_description: Adjust and customize buttonhole properties, including style, transformation angles, Z-offset, bind position, and 2D measurements for precise garment design.

title: Trim Grading
content: **New in 2024.2** #### **Apply grading rules to Trims added to Patterns. ** ** ** 1. Open trim to Pattern. 2. Create grading sizes or apply existing grading sizes.** ** 3. Select the trim in the 2D window using the ![Edit Grading On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37934564010265)**Grading** tool in the 2D toolbar. 4. Use the arrow keys or configure options as needed to edit grading rules. * Base Size cannot be edited. **📝****Note:** Grading rules applied to the trim only affect trim placement, not size.
content_description: Discover how to apply grading rules to trims in patterns with our new features in version 2024.2, enhancing your design precision and efficiency.

title: Edit Line (Avatar)
content: **List of Contents** Edit Line (Avatar) Use Line (Avatar) **Edit Line (Avatar) ** \- Edit the shapes and lines drawn with the **Line (Avatar)** tool. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021381848/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (Avatar)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Edit Line (Avatar). ** * **Add Point ** \- Edit by adding a Segment Point to Line (Avatar) using the right-click pop-up menu. \- Select the**Line(Avatar)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the **Line(Avatar)** where a Segment Point should be added. \- Then, Select Add Point. * **Add Curve Point ** \- Edit by adding a Curve Point ti Line (Avatar) using the right-click pop-up menu. \- Select the**Line(Avatar)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the **Line(Avatar)** where a Curve Point should be added. \- Then, Select Add Point. **** * **Flattening as Straight Line(ver4.1.0) ** \- Flatten selected lines straight by using the right-click pop-up menu. \- Select the**Line(Avatar)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Right click on the **Line(Avatar)** to be flattened as a straight line and select Flattening as Straight Line. ** Use Line (Avatar)** * **Select Point/Line** \- After selecting the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021381848/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (Avatar)** tool, hover over the line on the Avatar or the object in the 3D window. Click when the line is highlighted in light blue. \- When the line is properly selected, the line will be highlighted in yellow. \- Similarly, when the mouse is hovered over a point, only the point will be highlighted in light blue. Click once to select. \- The point will be highlighted in yellow. * **Edit Line/Shape** \- Edit lines by moving the points on the lines. \- Click and drag the point as the point moves along the mouse cursor. ** ** * **Delete** \- Delete the selected points and lines. \- Right click on the point to be deleted to access the pop-up menu. \- Select the **Delete** option. \- To delete a whole line or a shape, right click on the line or shape to access the pop-up menu. \- Select the **Delete** option. The selected line or the shape will be deleted. \- Or, when the desired item is selected, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to delete the selected item. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for using the Edit Line (Avatar) and Use Line (Avatar) tools in the 3D design environment, detailing functions such as editing, adding points, flattening lines, and deleting elements.
